subject: Post-demo: deployment fit & migration constraints for Medisys
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medisys.ai>, Bethany Li <bethany@medisys.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment fit & migration constraints for Medisys

Thanks for the demo time earlier — quick written recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and scope a short spike. I captured our notes below and a proposed next step.

Recap (what I heard)
- Current infra: on-prem/colocated GPU cluster (Triton + custom autoscaling), ~4x A100 nodes, serving a mix of chat+completion workloads.
- Primary blockers: PHI data handling (needs residency and strict KMS controls), procurement/regulatory review, and steady 200 qps peak with short spikes.
- Desired outcome: lower tail latency, predictable unit cost, and a migration plan that avoids user-facing risk.

Key technical constraints to confirm
- Is PHI the only reason for VPC/on-prem requirement, or are there additional regulatory/compliance controls (e.g., strict data residency in a VPC, audit log retention >1yr)?
- Do you require customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) or is a vendor-managed KMS acceptable for the POC?
- Expected latency SLO (p50/p95) and acceptable cold-start window for batch spikes?
- Are you open to a hybrid approach (Dedicated compute + customer VPC peering) during the migration window?

Proposed next step
- Can you share a short capacity snapshot (RPS, typical sequence length distribution, current token cost targets)? I referenced two attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (our compliance overview) and network_diagram.png (placeholder for how Redwood could peer).
- If comfortable, I'd like to schedule a 30-min infra handshake this week with your infra lead so Karthik can confirm peering/ops details.

Thanks — I want to make sure we recommend the least disruptive path. Will follow up with a short meeting link.

—
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF), network_diagram.png (PNG)

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medisys.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Bethany Li <bethany@medisys.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment fit & migration constraints for Medisys

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications inline.

Quick answers:
- PHI + regulatory auditability are both required. We must keep logs for 3 years and be able to provide audit trails.
- BYOK is mandatory for production; for a POC we can use vendor KMS if the keys are destroyed after the test and SOC2 evidence is provided.
- Target SLO: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 350ms for interactive flows; for batch inference p95 <= 1.2s.
- We are open to a hybrid approach — ideally dedicated GPUs with peering into our VPC (we run in us-west-2).

Background on our cluster: legacy Triton fronted by a custom queuing layer. Current steady-state ~120 qps; short bursts up to ~260 qps for a few minutes. I'll attach the last month's capacity_report.csv for your sizing.

Procurement/timeframe
- Security and procurement review scheduled for mid-November. If we can complete a POC (2 week spike) in October/early November, procurement can sign for Dedicated capacity with a November start.

Next steps from our side
- Please validate whether a Dedicated + VPC-peering option is something Redwood supports (we heard yes during the demo but want written confirmation).
- Karthik — can you propose the exact peering/egress requirements so our network team can pre-clear them?

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering | Medisys Health
Tom.Reynolds@medisys.ai | (206) 555-0199

Attachments: capacity_report.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medisys.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment fit & migration constraints for Medisys

Thanks Tom — good detail. A few narrow questions from infra so we can size the spike and confirm network options:

1) Network/peering
- Can you allow VPC peering with a customer-owned VPC in us-west-2 (we'll provide VPC CIDRs), or do you require transit via your corporate firewall (we need to know whether to support IP allowlists only)?

2) Keys & encryption
- For BYOK: do you have a supported KMS provider (AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing, or an HSM vendor)? We'll need the KMS ARN pattern to validate integration during the POC.

3) Model/serve details
- Typical sequence lengths (p50/p95) and the largest model family you expect to serve (e.g., 70B vs 13B). This affects cache and KV behavior.

4) Canary/rollback policy
- Are you comfortable with a canary routing policy (5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated during POC) or do you need a dark-launch mirror?

If useful, I can propose a 30-minute infra-only call tomorrow morning to walk through these with your network/security lead.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

On Tue, Sep 28, 2027 at 5:46 PM Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medisys.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications inline.
> ...

Cc: Bethany Li <bethany@medisys.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment fit & migration constraints for Medisys

Karthik — we can do the peering (VPC peering in us-west-2) and will provide the KMS ARN pattern (AWS KMS + CloudHSM) prior to the POC.

Confirmed: Medisys prefers Dedicated capacity deployed into our VPC with peering (Dedicated + private VPC topology). Production will require BYOK and extended audit retention; for the POC we accept vendor-managed KMS if keys are destroyed after.

Procurement timeline: security review mid-Nov; we'd like to run a 2-week spike the week of Oct 18 — can you confirm Redwood availability (dedicated nodes for that window) and a short SOW? We want as little friction as possible on our side.

Thanks — copying Bethany (procurement) to align on SOW and timing.

Tom
Head of Platform Engineering | Medisys Health

Attachments: none in this message (capacity_report.csv previously attached)
